nodes.name: Index Problem
nodes.content: Query performance degradation due to missing or inefficient indexes, causing full table scans

nodes.name: BGWriter Parameter Problem
nodes.content: Backend processes frequently flush dirty pages due to misconfigured bgwriter parameters

nodes.name: Shared Buffer Not Enough
nodes.content: Insufficient shared_buffers causing excessive disk reads and low cache hit ratio

nodes.name: Checkpoint Parameter Problem
nodes.content: Checkpoint operations causing I/O spikes due to misconfigured checkpoint parameters

nodes.name: WAL Parameter Problem
nodes.content: WAL accumulation or performance issues due to WAL configuration problems

nodes.name: Table Dead Tuple
nodes.content: Table bloat from accumulated dead tuples affecting query performance and disk usage

nodes.name: Statistics Expired
nodes.content: Outdated table statistics causing query planner to choose suboptimal execution plans

nodes.name: Lock Contention
nodes.content: Multiple sessions competing for locks causing performance degradation

nodes.name: High Memory Usage
nodes.content: Memory pressure or OOM condition affecting database performance

nodes.name: High CPU Usage
nodes.content: CPU saturation degrading overall database performance

nodes.name: Connection Storm
nodes.content: Sudden spike in active connections overwhelming the database

nodes.name: Suboptimal Join
nodes.content: Query using inefficient join order or algorithm causing performance issues

nodes.name: Missing Index Diagnosis
nodes.content: When queries perform Seq Scan on large tables, check for missing indexes on WHERE/JOIN columns. Use EXPLAIN to identify sequential scans, then CREATE INDEX on the filtered columns.

nodes.name: BGWriter Tuning
nodes.content: When backend processes flush dirty pages, bgwriter_lru_maxpages and bgwriter_lru_multiplier may be too low. Increase these parameters to allow bgwriter to handle more pages per round.

nodes.name: Shared Buffer Sizing
nodes.content: Low cache_hit_ratio indicates shared_buffers is too small. Recommended: 25% of system RAM. Check pg_stat_bgwriter for buffer allocation statistics.

nodes.name: Checkpoint Tuning
nodes.content: I/O spikes during checkpoints indicate checkpoint_completion_target too low or max_wal_size too small. Spread checkpoint writes over longer period.

nodes.name: WAL Configuration
nodes.content: WAL accumulation indicates wal_keep_size too large or archive_command failing. Check pg_stat_archiver and disk usage trends.

nodes.name: Vacuum Required
nodes.content: High dead tuple count indicates autovacuum is not keeping up. Check autovacuum_vacuum_threshold, autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor. Consider manual VACUUM on affected tables.

nodes.name: Statistics Update Required
nodes.content: Suboptimal query plans suggest outdated statistics. Run ANALYZE on affected tables. Check autovacuum_analyze_threshold settings.

nodes.name: Lock Resolution
nodes.content: Lock contention: identify blocking sessions via pg_stat_activity and pg_locks. Consider terminating long-running transactions or adjusting lock_timeout.

nodes.name: Memory Management
nodes.content: OOM conditions: check work_mem, maintenance_work_mem, shared_buffers sizing. Review dmesg for OOM killer events. Consider reducing max_connections or per-session memory.

nodes.name: CPU Diagnosis
nodes.content: High CPU: identify expensive queries via pg_stat_statements or topsql. Check for missing indexes causing excessive computation, or parallel query misconfiguration.

nodes.name: Connection Management
nodes.content: Connection storms: check max_connections setting, consider connection pooling (PgBouncer). Identify connection leak sources in application.

nodes.name: Join Optimization
nodes.content: Suboptimal joins: check join_collapse_limit, enable_hashjoin/enable_mergejoin settings. Update statistics and consider explicit join hints via SET commands.

nodes.name: EXPLAIN Analysis
nodes.content: Run EXPLAIN ANALYZE on slow queries to identify execution plan issues

attributes.sql_template: EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) SELECT * FROM pg_stat_user_tables WHERE n_dead_tup > 0 ORDER BY n_dead_tup DESC LIMIT 5

nodes.name: Active Session Analysis
nodes.content: Check pg_stat_activity for blocking queries and session states

attributes.sql_template: SELECT pid, state, wait_event_type, wait_event, query_start, left(query, 100) as query FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE state != 'idle' ORDER BY query_start LIMIT 20

nodes.name: Lock Analysis
nodes.content: Analyze lock contention via pg_locks

attributes.sql_template: SELECT l.pid, l.locktype, l.mode, l.granted, a.state, left(a.query, 80) as query FROM pg_locks l JOIN pg_stat_activity a ON l.pid = a.pid WHERE NOT l.granted LIMIT 10

nodes.name: BGWriter Statistics
nodes.content: Check bgwriter and checkpoint statistics

attributes.sql_template: SELECT checkpoints_timed, checkpoints_req, buffers_checkpoint, buffers_clean, buffers_backend, maxwritten_clean FROM pg_stat_bgwriter

nodes.name: Table Statistics
nodes.content: Check table-level statistics for dead tuples and sequential scans

attributes.sql_template: SELECT relname, n_dead_tup, n_live_tup, last_vacuum, last_autovacuum, last_analyze, seq_scan, idx_scan FROM pg_stat_user_tables ORDER BY n_dead_tup DESC LIMIT 10

nodes.name: Index Analysis
nodes.content: Check index usage statistics

attributes.sql_template: SELECT schemaname, relname, indexrelname, idx_scan, idx_tup_read FROM pg_stat_user_indexes ORDER BY idx_scan ASC LIMIT 10
